legal_basis: RBI Master Directions (loans), Indian Contract Act 1872 (Sec 27, Sec 74), and general Indian consumer-contract norms. No state-specific rental rules apply in this pack — the UI must show the amber 'Pan-India General Norms Only' badge.

rules.title: RBI Key Facts Statement (KFS) Disclosure

benchmark.typical_label: KFS must be provided before loan signing

statutory_citation.act: RBI Master Direction — Key Facts Statement (KFS) for Loans

rules.detection_hint: If this is a loan document and no KFS (all-in cost, APR, fees) is attached or referenced, flag it. The KFS is mandatory for regulated lenders before signing.

negotiation_ask.short_title: Ask for the RBI Key Facts Statement
negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could you share the RBI Key Facts Statement for this loan so I can see the all-in cost and fees before signing?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Under RBI's KFS mandate, a Key Facts Statement must be provided before signing. Please share it before I proceed.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: The Lender shall provide the Borrower with the RBI-mandated Key Facts Statement (KFS) disclosing the all-inclusive annualised rate, processing fees, and total cost of credit prior to execution.

rules.title: Post-Employment Non-Compete is Void in India

benchmark.typical_label: 0 months post-employment; only in-term restrictions are valid

statutory_citation.section: Section 27 — Agreement in restraint of trade

rules.detection_hint: If this is an offer letter or employment contract and it contains a post-employment non-compete restriction (any duration), flag it. Section 27 voids post-employment non-competes. In-term restrictions are generally enforceable.

negotiation_ask.polite_ask: I understand confidentiality and in-term restrictions are important, but could we remove the post-employment non-compete? Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act voids it, so it doesn't protect either of us.
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 voids post-employment non-competes as agreements in restraint of trade. Please remove Clause {clause_ref}, or limit it to confidentiality and in-term restrictions.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: This Agreement contains no post-employment non-compete restriction. The Employee's obligations are limited to confidentiality of proprietary information and non-solicitation of employees during employment, consistent with Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

rules.title: Specific Deposit Refund Timeline

benchmark.typical_label: 15–30 days after handover, with itemised deductions

statutory_citation.act: Indian Contract Act, 1872; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
statutory_citation.section: Unfair trade practice — open-ended deposit retention

rules.detection_hint: Flag if the agreement does not specify a refund deadline for any security deposit, or says the deposit will be refunded 'after deductions' without a time limit.

negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could we add a line that the deposit will be refunded within 15 days of handover, with any deductions listed in writing?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Clause {clause_ref} leaves the deposit refund open-ended. Please add a 15-day deadline after handover with an itemised deduction statement.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: Any refundable deposit shall be returned, after lawful and itemised deductions (if any), within fifteen (15) days of the counterparty handing over possession or completing the relevant handover obligations.

rules.title: One-Sided Penalty Without Counterpart

benchmark.typical_label: Penalties must apply symmetrically or be justified

rules.detection_hint: Flag clauses that impose a penalty on one party only (e.g. only the tenant, only the employee), with no equivalent obligation on the other party, especially where the penalty is disproportionate to any likely loss.

negotiation_ask.polite_ask: Could we make this penalty symmetric — the same rule applies to both sides — so it reads as a fair protection rather than a one-sided one?
negotiation_ask.firm_ask: Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act limits penalties to reasonable compensation. Clause {clause_ref} is one-sided and disproportionate. Please make it symmetric or reduce it to a reasonable estimate of actual loss.
negotiation_ask.replacement_wording: Any penalty under this Agreement shall apply symmetrically to both parties, and shall be limited to a reasonable estimate of the loss likely to result from the relevant breach, consistent with Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

expected_clauses.label: Specific deposit refund timeline
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: Open-ended refund language delays refunds after handover.

expected_clauses.label: Symmetric notice period
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: One-sided notice lets the stronger party exit without giving the weaker party time to plan.

expected_clauses.label: Dispute resolution and jurisdiction
expected_clauses.why_it_matters: Without a specified forum, disputes default to the drafting party's home court, which may be far away.
